column1: // Constructions of the rewrite layer (docs/rule-language.md, 구문 표): the Korean of a word picked

// A family is declared once by "//= FAMILY <TAB> after PASS STAGE [<TAB> guard CONDITION] <TAB> what
// it is for" and runs after the text pass PASS, the families after one pass in the order of their
// STAGE numbers (gaps of 10 leave room between). A word on which the guard is false tries none of
// the family's rows. Its rows are ID <TAB> SPEC <TAB> CONDITION <TAB> ACTIONS
// <TAB> NOTE, ID being cx:FAMILY:PRIO. On each word from the left, the first row of the family by

column3: The verb describes no noun after it, but a formal noun of noun.clause (also after an auxiliary: 覗かれていた気がした), and no verb follows it in the sentence but an auxiliary of its て form or one after such a formal noun, which belongs to the clause around it (見られている気がした).

A dictionary word that is the passive of a dictionary verb, read with 어지다, 되다, a potential or an honorific, which no Korean reader uses with an object; not before いる, whose 어 있다 the active verb cannot take (知られている 알려져 있다).

A passive verb that no Korean passive word reads yet (an analysed passive, or a dictionary word that is the passive of a dictionary verb read with 어지다, 되다, a potential or an honorific: 使われた 사용되었다, 見られた 볼 수 있었다), with a person before に as its agent an object of を in its clause and no subject or topic (が, は, も, って) before the に, is the act of that person: the に is the subject (이)가, with a pronoun in its subject form, and the verb is active, a dictionary word being written as its verb (弟に手紙を破られた 남동생이 편지를 찢었다, 父に傘を使われた 아버지가 우산을 사용했다, 俺に頭を撫でられる 내가 머리를 쓰다듬는다). A verb of seeing (verb.perception) needs no object: what is seen is the one it happens to (誰かに見られている 누군가가 보고 있다, 彼女に覗かれている 그녀가 들여다보고 있다), unless Korean reads it with a passive word of its own (母に見られた 어머니에게 보였다). Not other verbs without an object (母に叱られた 어머니에게 야단맞았다), nor when the verb describes a noun after it that is no noun.clause (彼女に別れ話を切り出された情けないヤツ keeps the passive) or another verb that is no auxiliary of its て form follows it in the sentence (吸われ、自らも吸血鬼化した keeps the passive).

A causative-passive verb that may be an act one is made to do: analysed, or a dictionary row of verb.causative-passive (the other dictionary verbs in させられ say a feeling: ドキリとさせられる 깜짝 놀라다).

The に after a person before a causative-passive verb (読まされる, a dictionary verb in させられ or one of verb.causative-passive: 待たされる), not one that asks or denies, which is the potential (食らわせられるか), nor one read as a Korean passive in 받다 (하도록 강요받다), which takes 에게; with no other に, no は, が or から, no verb, no adjective but one before the noun it describes and no punctuation between, names who made it happen: 때문에 (兄に待たされた 형 때문에 기다리게 되었다). When the verb is an act one was made to do (forced-act) and no adverb of adverb.forcing stands in the clause, the 억지로 of that act follows it (母に野菜を食べさせられた 어머니 때문에 억지로 야채를 먹었다).

column3: A causative-passive verb (読まされる, a dictionary row of verb.causative-passive, or させられ after a noun) after a causer that causer-ni read 때문에 억지로, or 때문에 with an adverb of adverb.forcing in the clause, not one that asks or denies, which is the potential, nor one of something one goes through (undergone-verb), is the act one was made to do: the active verb (母に本を読まされた 어머니 때문에 억지로 책을 읽었다, 父に勉強させられた 아버지 때문에 억지로 공부했다). Its て form that no auxiliary follows links the act to what came of it, 어서 (先輩に無理やり飲まされて 선배 때문에 억지로 마셔서). Without a causer it stays 게 되다. The させられ after a noun reads 하게 되다 (L4554: 心配させられた 걱정하게 되었다), after a noun of something one undergoes whose Korean takes 당하다 (ko-noun.cp-danghada) it is 당하다 (解雇させられた 해고당했다), after one that takes 받다 (ko-noun.passive-batda) 받다 (検査させられた 검사받았다), and after a noun of a change that befalls one (noun.cp-change) with no object を before it in its clause it is 되다 (孤立させられた 고립되었다). A causative-passive whose ending already says 게 되다 (ことになる) drops its own (読まされることになった 읽게 되었다, 退院させられることになった 퇴원하게 되었다).

column3: What stops the search from a giver before に to its verb: a particle of another role, a mark, or a verb that is no adjective in く.

The してもら read 받다 (지도를 받다, 설명받다) is 해 주다 when a person before it, with に read 에게 and no other に, no は, が or から, no verb but an adjective in く and no punctuation between, does it for the speaker, with no subject or topic (が, は, も, って) before the person in the clause: the giver then becomes the subject (benefactive-provider). Not right after a verbal noun of noun.receive-verbal, whose 받다 is one Korean verb (紹介してもらった 소개받았다). After an adverb, an adjective in く or a verb in ように with no object を before it, it is 해 주다 too (優しくしてもらった 다정하게 해 주었다), but not after よく (잘 대접받다). A もら read 달라고 하다 (a request) after a causative is the plain 주다: the causative asks leave, not a favour (見極めさせてもらおう).

The に after a person read 에게 before a verb with もらう (also 貰う, aux.morau), or with いただく read 주시다, with no other に, no は, が or から, no verb (an adjective in く may stand there) and no punctuation between, names the giver: the subject (이)가, with a pronoun in its subject form (누가), or (은)는 for には. Not when the verb before もらう is a causative (相談をさせてもらう). A に read (이)가 before a もら read 달라고 하다 (a request: 作ってもらえ, 作ってもらおう) is the one asked, 에게.

column3: A は, が or も after a noun that names someone the speaker honours (先生は, 部長が).
An honoured subject or topic before the word in its sentence (先生は…と言われた), also before a bracketed quote the word follows, with a comma or nothing between (先生は「静かに」と言われた), whose 言われる is respectful.
A は or が before the word in its sentence after a noun that names someone the speaker honours (先生は来週テストだと言われた): the sayer, which a も after a quoted title is not (部長も…なんて言われて).

The 言われ is a past or a て form that is no condition or concession, no state (ている), nothing long said with no person who said it or was told it (この森には神がいると言われてきた; not 母に…, 彼は…), describes no noun after it and has no comma after it, asks nothing, and no honoured person says it: what is said of everyone (と言われる, と言われ、, と言われた時代) stays 하다.

column4: The 言われ after a quote that L5324 read as the active 하다 (嫌いだって言われた 싫다고 했다) is what the speaker was told: 말을 듣다, with the quoting ending before it written as the modifier (싫다는 말을 들었다), in a past, a て form or a negative past (spec GRM-3872); not after a condition or concession, in a state, a non-past or a question, or with an honoured person as the sayer.

column4: A もら or もらえ after a causative in て with no person but the speaker in に before it is the speaker's act with leave (spec GRM-44). A もら that ends the sentence goes into the verb's ending: 겠습니다, 겠다, 겠어 (わ, よ, ぞ), 게요, 게 (ね) for the present, the plain past for もらった and 었어 for もらったよ and もらったわ (やらせてもらいます 하겠습니다, 読ませてもらった 읽었다). So does the ます of a word of verb.permission-word (使わせてもらいます 사용하겠습니다). A もらえ or いただけ in ますか or ませんか asks leave: 어도 될까요, the speaker in に before it the subject; after another person in に it asks that person, 게 해 주실 수 있을까요 (俺にやらせてもらえますか 내가 해도 될까요; permission-request has the causatives that hold もらえませんか or いただけ). A count word whose counter needs a cue (着, 脚, 服, 丁, 膳, 両, 張, 足, 二輪 and 三輪 by a flower, 一機 by a machine) is a count only next to a noun of that class, with が, は, を or も between but not で; 基, 筋, 曲, 枚 are counts after a noun with が, は, を or も, or before a verb, だけ, ずつ, しか, も, ほど, くらい or the end. Words like 一足先, 一着 (a placing), 三脚 (a tripod), 一服 (a break), 一筋縄 and 三位一体 stay.

column3: Readings that inverted or garbled the meaning of a line: a について that the word stage read as arrival after a place is 대해 when the first verb after it in its clause, before any comma, is one of speaking, thinking or knowing, before の, は, も or で, or ending a line; 巡る after を and a noun of an issue, or before a dispute, is 둘러싸다 (和平案を巡って 평화안을 둘러싸고), not 돌다; きる right after an ichidan stem is 다 and the verb (疲れきった 다 지친), not 切る; a godan e-row form before など and と is the imperative (帰れなどと 돌아가라); a と read as a condition before the past or て form of 知る, 分かる, 気づく is what was found out, -다는 걸; 宿す of what is no child is 품다; よ and a comma after a title that opens its clause calls it, (이)여 (提督よ、 제독이여), but for kin, a noun with の and alarm cries; ようとして before くれる is -려고 해 주다; かわす with no object that ends its clause or is a て, つつ or continuative form is 피하다; みたく after a noun is 처럼; the と of an adjective before a subject and a verb of thinking or saying quotes it, and a く adjective right before such a verb is -게 (強く思う 강하게 생각한다); だけに after a person before a verb is 에게만; 仕方ない and しかない before a comma end their clause (어쩔 수 없다,); 取り上げられる with an object of を and no news medium in its clause is 빼앗기다 and 弾かれる after a weapon, a blow or a guard and before no tune or instrument 튕기다.

column3: Misreadings a web novel example showed: ある right before a noun that is the subject of いる or ある is 어느, not 있는 (王国にはある王女がいる 왕국에는 어느 왕녀가 있다); が after a person before 見 read as its potential, with no を in the clause, marks what is seen, (을)를 (味方が見られない 아군을 볼 수 없는); 知れ after a quote and before a comma and a name is the order 알아라 (貴様だと知れ、ユフィリア 네놈이라고 알아라, 유필리아); など before a と that ends the utterance is (이)라니 (解消などと……！ 해소라니……!), など ending an exclaimed utterance after a noun is 같은 건, なんかが after a noun 같은 게; the spelled-out 곱슬곱슬 of ちりちり before する or an adjective is the prickling 찌릿찌릿; そこまで before an adjective, する or やる (not a verb of going or reaching, そこまで行きたい 거기까지 가고 싶다), or before a noun and a denied predicate, is the degree 그렇게까지; どういう事 after これは, after のは or after 一体 asks what is going on, 어떻게 된 일; あれ before a comma and もしかして or まさか is the interjection 어라; ように and して before a main verb is the manner 듯이 (支えられるようにして立つ 의지하듯이 서다); a clause in 다고 before という and a noun is -다는 (促すという目的 촉진한다는 목적); a role noun before に and a predicative 相応しい is (으)로, へと before 勤しむ or 励む is 에, に before 嫉妬する and 耐える is (을)를 and 耐える is 견디다, に before a noun and があ is 에; が before an embedded question read 를 is (이)가, なのか before a particle is 인지.
The quoting ending before an emptied という and a noun (온다고 하는 이야기 온다는 이야기).

column3: A word that needs a negative stands before the verb in its clause (何も言わないと, 誰も来ないと): the ない is a negative of its own, not the condition of an obligation.
The いかない of an idiom after は or も, that it does not go so (そうはいかないと, わけにはいかないと), not going.
A verb of saying or vowing follows in the sentence (負けないと…心に誓った, 笑わないと…そう思っていた): the ない is what was said or vowed, not the condition of an obligation.
A verb of a state one is in or comes to without doing it (分かる, できる, 間に合う, 見つかる): no one is told to do it, so its ないと is the condition or what one expects (わからないと, しばらくは見つからないと…).

The sentence goes on to a verb not in て that asks nothing: what the condition leads to (急がないと……きっと後悔する, そうしないと……一緒にいられなくなる), not a new question (夕飯食わないと……みんな何食べる？), what comes after a space, a conjunction or an interjection that starts another sentence (気を付けないと‥‥ 川内さん、行きましょう, 助けないと……でもどうやれば) or another obligation (つけないと……忘れて、いかないと).

A verb read in one word with its negative before ないと (しな 하지 않다, くれな 주지 않다, していな 하고 있지 않다), not a copula or すぎない in it (好きじゃないと) and not before the rest of an obligation or what follows from the condition (しないと……だめ, しないと…わかんない).
A closing ね or な ends the sentence after the word.

column4: A verb read in one word with its negative (しな 하지 않다, 寝な 잠을 자지 않다, くれな 주지 않다, こな 오지 않다, していな 하고 있지 않다, いかな 가지 않다) before a ないと that ends the sentence says what one must do, as GRM-3565 reads a verb and な (spec GRM-3610): it is read again as that verb, -아야 한다 (運動しないと。 운동해야 한다, 少し寝ないと！ 조금 잠을 자야 해!, 寝ててくんないと！ 자고 있어 줘야 해!), and -아야지 before a closing ね or な (準備しないとね 준비해야지). Not before a comma or a question mark (気にしないと？ quotes), after a word that needs a negative (何もしないと), before a pause after which the sentence goes on to what follows from the condition (なにもしないと……きっと、後悔する), nor いかない after は (そうはいかないと).

column3: More words and clause links the web novel examples misread: a verb in かけ with の and a noun after it is the act under way, -는 (死にかけの脳細胞 다 죽어가는 뇌세포), and a subject の before it is 의; よか between a noun and マシ, いい or a comparison is 보다는 (泣き顔よかマシだ 우는 얼굴보다는 낫다); an adjectival noun before なんかじゃない is -ㄴ 것도 아니다 (ユニークなんかじゃない 독특한 것도 아니야); the greeting 안녕 standing as a sentence in polite speech is 안녕하세요; 以来の, 以上の or a time and からの before 付き合い is 알고 지내는 사이; an age in 歳で with まだ and a comma is 세이고; a verb read -가다 before くる comes, -오다 (駆け寄ってくる 달려온다), but not 行く, 出かける or a verb after a purpose に, which go and come back, and なって or なく before くる of a change is 되다 (感じなくなってきた 느끼지 않게 되었다); a present verb before 事になる or 事となる, not いう, is -게 되다 (転生する事となる 전생하게 된다); 事により after a verb is -ㅁ으로써; に before 進化 or 変化 after a being or a form (change-result-before) is (으)로; 風呂 before に and 沈める is 욕조; 目視で is 육안으로 and 真っ青な顔 새파랗게 질린 얼굴; やってくれ after a て form, and してやってくれ after a verbal noun, is 줘; a person, の事 and a comma before a predicate that takes a person as its object (person-object-after) is (을)를; あの世 is 저세상; 駄目か is 안 되나; こっちは after a comma at the end is 이쪽은; の between a noun and 無さそう is (이)가; たく after a comma at the end is 참나; 続けて opening a sentence is 이어서; 勘弁して欲しい is 봐줬으면 하다; 顔して before a comma is 얼굴을 하고; な ending an exclamation after a noun or an adjectival noun is -네 or (이)야.
A predicate after the word, before any other conjugating word or the end of the sentence, takes a person as its object: 好き, 嫌い, 忘れる, 分かる, 知る, 見る, 信じる, 頼む by their base form, よろしく, 幸せにする and 自慢する.

The noun before the word, not a suffix (たち, さん) or a part of the body, is a being or a form a thing turns into: a creature or a name, or a katakana noun, neither of place or time (ロンドン, クリスマス, ターン), a noun of noun.change-result, or a name in brackets.

The 進化 or 変化 with する after it describes 様子, 部分, 感じ, 気配, 形跡, ところ or 点 (also ところ before は, が or も read into the ending of する; したところだ is not): a change in the noun before に, not what it turns into (体に変化した様子はない).

column3: Clause shapes whose Korean flipped the meaning. A quote in って or と, or そう, before 言ってる with でしょ or だろ (also ん) that ends the sentence, or だろうが that ends it, is the retort 말하잖아 (子供じゃないって言ってるでしょ！ 아이가 아니라고 말하잖아!), not 말하고 있지 or 말하는 걸까; the guess だろう stays (来るって言ってるだろうと思う); a ん form before a question mark asks to confirm and stays, as does a question word (何て言ってるんだろう). The same before a closing んだ, んだよ or のよ that ends the sentence says what one means, 말하는 거야, and after a quoted imperative it is -라니까 (やめろって言ってんだよ 그만두라니까) (spec GRM-3722). A verb in its dictionary form with な that ends the sentence after a verb in ながら is the prohibition -지 마 (食べながら話すな 먹으면서 이야기하지 마), not the observation 구나, unless the verb is potential, よく stands before it, a は topic other than you is named, or the line opens with a word of wonder (へえ、) (spec GRM-3723). いらっしゃいませんか after 一緒に, or after 遊びに, invites, 오시지 않겠습니까 (遊びにいらっしゃいませんか 놀러 오시지 않겠습니까), not 계시지 않습니까 (spec LEX-4600). An の the rules read as a space before an abstract or relational noun of noun.abstract-relation is 의 (言葉の意味 말의 의미), unless the noun before it is itself after an の, is a demonstrative of a side (そっちの意味 그쪽 의미) or makes a Korean compound with it (主従の関係 주종 관계), or another noun follows (関係組織) (spec GRM-3721). A noun with じゃなくて or ではなくて before another noun, or before a comma or a pause and a noun, is the contrast 아니라 (私じゃなくて妹です 내가 아니라 여동생입니다), not the reason 아니어서; before an evaluation or a feeling (良かった, 残念, がっかり) it stays the reason (人じゃなくて良かった 사람이 아니어서 다행이다) (spec GRM-3724). Also: そう言ってるでしょ is 그렇게 말하잖아; いらっしゃいませんか after a place one goes to with に (うちに, パーティーに), or after a place in a clause with an inviting word (今度, ぜひ), invites, unless the clause has a は or が subject or 今, まだ, もう (LEX-4600); じゃなくて before a feeling (嬉しい, 悲しい) is the reason 아니어서 (GRM-3724); a verb one keeps doing (verb.keep-doing: 見る, 見張る, 寝る) in ていないと that ends the sentence is what one must keep doing, 봐야 한다 (GRM-3725). A てもらいたい read 주고 싶다, or ていただきたい read 주시고 싶다, is what one wishes someone did for one (母に買ってもらいたい), 사 줬으면 좋겠다, not 사 주고 싶다 (GRM-3726). 乗せられ read 넘어가다 (話に乗せられた) is that verb itself, 넘어갔다, not 넘어가졌다 (LEX-4607). Also: より read 에서 before a はない is the comparison 보다 (GRM-3903); それと opening a sentence is 그리고 (GRM-3904); ところ after 妙な, 変な and the like before ある is a trait, 점 (LEX-4804); 高く before a sound verb is 높게 (LEX-4805). そうじゃなくて opening what is said, or after a comma or pause, corrects it, 그게 아니라 (LEX-4800). A person with が before 好きな, 嫌いな or 欲しい that describes a noun is the one who likes or wants, (이)가 (コウくんが好きなこと 코우 군이 좋아하는 일, 君が欲しい下着 네가 갖고 싶은 속옷) (GRM-3905). やる after ても is 하다, and について before a verb of talking or knowing is 에 대해 (LEX-4808). Quotes and conditions: a たって before 噂 or 話 is the quote 었다는 (見かけたって噂 봤다는 소문); ろうと after a question word concedes, -든 (何が起ころうと 뭐가 일어나든); 誰って echoes, 누구라니; ませんと is the condition 않으면 (GRM-3910); a noun with ってもの before だ is (이)라는 것 (LEX-4809). Sentence ends: てみせる said in speech (polite or 해체) resolves, 보이겠다 (愛してみせます 사랑해 보이겠습니다); narration keeps 보인다; a verb of verb.offer in るよ offers, -ㄹ게 (奢るよ 한턱낼게) (GRM-3911).
The ending of 좋다 after -지 말았으면, as a wish (좋겠어, 좋겠습니다).
The ending of 보이다 in てみせる, a resolve (보이겠습니다, 보이겠어).
The 言 of 言ってる after a quote in って or と, or after そう, with no question word before it.

column3: Nouns whose sense the words right around them show. 柄 right after a katakana word is a pattern, 무늬 (カボチャ柄の服 호박무늬의 옷), and 柄 before じゃ or では is one's nature, 성격 (そんな柄じゃねえ 그런 성격이 아니야). 始末 right after a verb at the end of a sentence is the sorry pass it came to, 지경 (追いかけていく始末 뒤쫓아 가는 지경), and before 出来 or させ it is getting rid of, 처리. 元 after a katakana name or a person and の is being with them, 곁, before まで or を, and being under them, 밑, before で (ハンスの元まで 한스의 곁까지). 舐める forbidden (舐めるな, 舐めんな), cursed (舐めやがって) or before かかる is looking down on, 얕보다, not licking. 弾く read as playing music is knocking away, 튕기다, only on a clear cue: its object or what it is done with is a blow, a weapon, a guard, a bullet, a coin, a ball, a finger, water, light or a liquid (シールドで弾いた 쉴드로 튕겼다), it comes before 飛ばす, 落とす or 出す, or it is passive with no instrument or tune in the line; an object it does not know stays 연주하다 (ゾナーテを弾こうか 소나타를 연주할까). 拝む one can (拝める, 拝めた) or wants to (拝みたい), or with 目 just before it, is getting to see, 보다, not praying (この目で拝める 이 눈으로 볼 수 있다). ついている beside someone (傍, そば, 側) is staying by them, 붙어 있다, not arriving, and おそば there is 곁, not noodles (おそばについていながら 곁에 붙어 있으면서). 前に, not after の, before a verb of stepping or thrusting out (踏み出す, 乗り出す, こぼれる, and 出る after 一歩) is forward, 앞으로 (一歩前に出た 한 걸음 앞으로 나왔다; spec LEX-4901).

column3: Common words whose usual sense the words right around them show. 一人 right after a person or another noun (柏木一人しかいない 카시와기 혼자밖에 없다, 自分一人じゃ 자기 혼자서는), or before だと, じゃ, では, ぼっち, なの？ or になる (not after の: 最後の一人になる), is being alone, 혼자, not the count 한 사람; after あと, 残り, 最後, うち, 誰か and the like, or before の, くらい or だけ, it stays a count (spec LEX-4810). 頃 after a noun and の is that time of life or of an event, 때, and the の drops (ガキの頃 꼬마 때, ６歳の頃 6세 때), and so is 頃 after いい (いい頃だ 좋은 때다); after 最初, 初め, 終わり, a month, a year, a time of day (東雲, 夕暮れ) and after その or あの, it stays 무렵 (spec LEX-4811). 命 with は, を, が, も or なんて after a person's の (not 人々の, 他人の, nor a person a clause describes), この or その is a life one can lose, 목숨 (私の命なんて 내 목숨 같은 건); 命の before a noun (命の恩人, 命の危険) and 命に別状 stay 생명 (spec LEX-4812). しっかり before a verb of holding (握る, 掴む, 抱く, つかまる) is 꽉, and before another verb or a noun of doing with する it is 제대로 (しっかり治してね 제대로 치료해); before する itself it stays (spec LEX-4813). もう opening what is said and followed by an exclamation mark, a small つ, a long mark, さ or ったら, but not by a pause, is the exasperated 정말 (もう！ありがと！ 정말! 고마워!) (spec LEX-4814). 気持ち right after の, その or あの is what one feels for someone or means, 마음 (本当の気持ち 진정한 마음, その気持ち 그 마음), but before いい, 良い, 悪い or か, or after a person a clause describes (やってきた俺の気持ち, how one felt then), it stays 기분 (spec LEX-4815). しっかり before a verb of remembering or knowing (覚える, 認識, 暗記), 働く, つける, ある or いる stays 확실히. 違う that ends the sentence after それは, そりゃ or そいつは denies, 아니다 (それは違うよ！ 그건 아니야!), not before の nor asked (spec LEX-4816). 付き合う after も that ends the sentence is keeping someone company, 어울리다 (俺も付き合うわ 나도 어울릴게) (spec LEX-4817). 止めて, 止めなさい, 止めてよ or 止めてください with no object in を that ends the sentence is 그만하다 (止めて！ 그만해!); 止める after のを or ことを is 그만두다, and after a pronoun, a kin word or an honoured person and を it is 말리다 (兄上を止める 형님을 말리다) (spec LEX-4818). 方 after 最後の, 最初の, 終わりの or 始めの is that time, 무렵; 方 before へ after an adjective is 쪽 with (으)로; 方 after そういった or 見知らぬ, or before が or は and おられる or いらっしゃる, is the honoured person 분 (spec LEX-4819). 本当 before だね, ですね, だな or じゃん agrees in surprise, 정말 (本当だね 정말이네), and 本当 before a comma is the adverb 정말; 本当だ and 本当なら stay 사실 (spec LEX-4611). 特に with a 없다 (ない, ありません, いない, なし, 何も) that describes no noun, before any other predicate or comma of its clause, is 특별히 (特に用事がなさそう 특별히 용무가 없을 것 같아); with none it stays 특히 (spec LEX-4612). 所 after a person and の before に or へ, and ところ there before へ, is going to that person, 에게, and 所 and の drop, but not before いる or ある (友人の所に来ました 친구에게 왔습니다), as ところ before に already reads (spec LEX-4613). こと or 事 read 일 after a quoting って or という is what is meant, 것, and that って is (이)라는 (勝ちって事で 승리라는 것으로), but 는 after a copula (嘘だったってことか 거짓말이었다는 건가), and not before になる, and so is 事 after そういう or どういう, not before の; after 何の asked or ending the sentence it is 말 (なんのこと？ 무슨 말?); 一つ before a sigh or a cough is 한 번 (spec LEX-4614). ちょっと opening what is said before a pause that ends it is 잠깐 (やっ、ちょっと…… 얏, 잠깐……), and いっぱい before a verb that fills nothing (not 入る, 溢れる, 詰まる, 満ちる, 並ぶ, 集まる, 溜まる, 咲く), or a noun with する, and not after a comma or a pause, is 많이 (いっぱい、愛してね 많이, 사랑해) (spec LEX-4615). する right after 気 that そんな or another adnominal describes, or after 嫌な予感, with the particle dropped is feeling it, 들다, and 気 there is 생각이 (そんな気しない？ 그런 생각이 들지 않아?) (spec LEX-4616). あと before a number or a count of times or of time (数秒, 二日, 何回) is how much is left, 앞으로; あと after a list in と or や and a comma adds one more, 그리고 (ご飯と、あと特製ジャーキー 밥과, 그리고 특제 육포), and so does あと standing alone before a period (spec LEX-4617). 気付く read 깨닫다 and negated (気付かない, 気付いていない), not after a に nor ことに, is not noticing, 알아차리지 못하다 (気付かなかったの？ 알아차리지 못했어?) (spec LEX-4618). まったく with a negative before the next comma, て or わけ of its clause is 전혀 (not a partial まったく…わけではない), and まったく opening what is said before a pause, a mark, もう or the end, not as the answer after いえ or いや, is the sigh 정말이지; 開 read 열다 with a noun and が or は right before it, or as 開いた before a noun, with no object in を and not asked or offered, is 열리다 (ドアは開いてた 문은 열려 있었어); の中で after a room, a vehicle, a box or another place one is inside (電車, 部屋, 結界) is 안에서 (電車の中で 전차 안에서), and a 近づく one wants, does while doing another thing, goes on doing (ていく) or is told not to do (近づくな) is 다가가다 (近づこう 다가가자) (spec LEX-4620). 前 right after 二人 to 十人, not before に, で or へ, is the portions of food, 인분, and the number goes to digits (四人前 4인분); にできる after a noun with an object in を before it in its clause is making that object the noun, (으)로 할 수 있다 (後ろ盾に出来れば 후원자로 할 수 있으면) (spec LEX-4621). スキ in katakana standing as the whole predicate at the end (キミがスキ 네가 좋아) is 好き, 좋아, and as a predicate with an ending (スキだけど, スキです, スキな) 좋아하다; before に or で, where a predicate reading would take them as its ending, it is an opening, 빈틈 (一瞬のスキに 순간의 빈틈에, わずかなスキで 약간의 빈틈으로), but スキになる stays liking (좋아하게), スキで after が, also with だい between, is 좋아서 and after は, も, を, こと or a bare だい 좋아해서, おスキに is 좋을 대로 and スキにする 마음대로 (spec LEX-4622). この手の before 中 or 上 is the speaker's hand, 이 손 (この手の中に 이 손 안에), not this kind (spec LEX-4622). 全く read 전혀 opening a line before a pause or a mark is the sigh 정말이지; 目下 not before a particle is now, 지금, not a subordinate; 本当なら with はず, べき, のに or ところ later in its sentence is what should have been, 원래라면 (spec LEX-4622). 承りました (not 承りましてよ) opening a line or a quote, with nothing before it, is the answer 알았습니다; 抜かせ opening a line is 웃기지 말아라; くそが or クソが opening a line or after a pause or a mark, before a mark, っ or the end, is the curse 젠장 (not クソが付く); いわく right after a noun is 왈 (not いわく付き); 早 before a number is 벌써 (早２年 벌써 2년; spec LEX-4625). 最後は before a clause with a verb, not となる, tells how it ended, 마지막에는 (最後はこうなる 마지막에는 이렇게 된다); 扱う after a manner (乱暴に, 大切に, 上手に) or as 扱える is handling, 다루다 (spec LEX-4624). 今度 after また, or with a plan, an offer or a request later in its sentence (今度また…しよ, 今度見てみるかい), is next time, 다음에, not 今度こそ or 今度は (spec LEX-4623). 並ぶ read 늘어서다 before a verb of walking, sitting, lying or standing is side by side, the adverb 나란히 alone (並んで立っていた 나란히 서 있었다); asked for or proposed (並んでください, 並ぼう, 並んで！) with no subject before it in its clause, it is people queuing, 줄을 서다 (早く並んで 빨리 줄을 서) (spec LEX-4623). 支える after a falling, stumbling or swaying in its sentence is holding a person up, 부축하다 (spec LEX-4623).

column3: Verbs whose sense the words around them show. 散って before いく or いった, with no flower, leaf, spark, snow, light or life in the sentence, is people scattering, 흩어지다 (みんなが散っていく 모두가 흩어져 간다), not falling, 지다. 聞いて before き or 来, with no object marked を before it in its clause (back to a comma or a verb) and not before もらう, is asking, 묻다 (投げやりに聞いてきた 무책임하게 물어 왔다; spec LEX-4902). 流す with 水で, お湯で or シャワーで just before it, or one adverb between, is washing, 씻다 (顔を水で流した 얼굴을 물로 씻었다; spec LEX-4904).

column3: Adverbs and verbs whose sense the words around them show. A 引く denied with no object in its clause and nothing that is drawn (a cold, a line, a trigger, a lot) before it is not backing down, 물러서지 않다 (一度言い出したら引かないタイプ 한 번 말을 꺼내면 물러서지 않는 타입). ずっと right after より, よりも or ほうが, or before マシ, 前から, 昔から, 上, 下 or 奥, compares or measures a distance, 훨씬, not 계속 (思ったよりもずっと大きな 생각했던 것보다도 훨씬 큰). イヤ opening a line or a quote before a comma that is not followed by です, だ or なの turns the speech, 아니 (イヤ、違うから 아니, 아니니까), and どうした right before the person spoken to asks what is wrong, 무슨 일이야 (どうしたお前ら 무슨 일이야, 너희들; spec LEX-4903).

column3: The て of かける after に with a から before it in its clause spans a stretch, 걸쳐 (ウエストから尻山にかけて). A かける right after the continuative of a verb, not one of verb.kakeru-directed, is an act begun and not finished. After a change that befalls the subject (verb.kakeru-unwilled) or a passive, its past that ends the clause or is taken by こと, ところ, の or せい nearly happened, (으)ㄹ 뻔하다 (流されかけた 떠밀릴 뻔했다, パニックになりかけたが 패닉이 될 뻔했지만); before another noun, in ている and in its other forms it is the change going on, 어 가다 (沈みかけた夕日 가라앉아 가던 석양, 忘れかけている 잊어 가고 있다). After a verb done on purpose it is the act one set out to do, (으)려고 하다 (言いかけた 말하려고 했다), and its て before a pause is 다 말고 (歩きかけて、 걷다 말고). The passive of a かける read 걸다, not in ている, is 걸리다 (持ち手にかけられた木札 손잡이에 걸린 목찰), but with an object を it is 걸치다 (テーブルクロスをかけられた机). After glasses in the line it is 쓰다 (メガネ…あ、私かけてた).

The 助かる is past (助かった, 助かりました).

助かる with no word of life, wounds or rescue (word.survival) in its sentence is help or relief, not surviving: not past, not denied, not wished and with no person as its subject it is 도움이 되다 (お茶、助かるわ 차, 도움이 돼; 依頼人がまた助かるかも keeps 살아나다), its past with no subject in が or だけ right before it in its clause is relief, 살다 (助かった 살았다, 手伝ってくれて助かりました 도와줘서 살았습니다). column3: Words the web novel examples misread. 成 after a noun and には is 되다 and the には (은)는 (デザイナーには成れない 디자이너는 될 수 없다). A sentence-initial もっとも with no comma is 가장 before an adjective, an adverb or a word that describes a noun (大きな, 人気のある, 効果的な) and the caveat 다만 before anything else but a verb (もっともある程度の知識がないと 다만 어느 정도의 지식이 없으면), not 무엇보다. 目を向ける after a modifier (an の or な, or an adjective) is 눈길을 보내다 (奇異の目を向けない 기이의 눈길을 보내지 않는다), not 눈길을 돌리다, which reads as looking away. A quoted 「…」 with が before 取れる came off, 빠지다. いくら with the か of a question before a noun or predicate other than one of knowing, asking, checking, seeing or counting is the amount 조금 (いくらか若返らせて 조금 젊어지게). 止めておく with no を or も object right before it is 그만두다. 独り言を言う is 혼잣말을 하다. 中 after the の of a first- or second-person pronoun is 안 with the pronoun 내, 제, 네 (俺の中 내 안, 私の中で 내 안에서), not 나중 or 나 중에서. 思い read 생각 before する, after a modifier, is 경험 (そういった思いはしたくない 그런 경험은 하고 싶지 않다); させる keeps it. ある right after a quotation in と says what is written, 적혀 있다 (揚げたとあった 튀겼다고 적혀 있었다, スキルポイント１０とあった 스킬 포인트 10이라고 적혀 있었다), not とある before a noun (a certain). 最後に after an の is the place, 마지막에. ラフな before clothing is 편한. に困る after a person is 때문에 곤란해하다. する after a heard sound (音, 足音, 物音 and the like, not 録音 or 発音) and smells with が, は or も is 나다 (足音がした 발소리가 났다, 音はしない 소리는 나지 않는다). じゃなく and ではなく before anything but なる or a verb of seeming (感じる, 思える, 見える, 聞こえる), and not after でも, are 아니라, not 아니게 (自室じゃなく荒野 자기 방이 아니라 황야). 駄目か, ダメか read 안된가 is 안 되나, and 안 돼 before a question mark. ちゃう before a question mark is -어 버려?, not -어 버리는?. なんか read 무슨 after a particle is the adverb 뭔가 with a space (最後のはなんか違う 마지막은 뭔가 다르다); after the に of a person (에게) or と with a negative within five words it belittles the noun, 따위 (other nouns with に are nado-dismissive's) (お前になんか負けない 너 따위에게 지지 않는다), and 무슨 with a space before 理由, わけ, 原因, 文句 or の. A verb in its dictionary form with に and a comma is -건대 (推測するに、 추측하건대,). The の read (이)가 before a verb row that holds its own noun and が or に (波にさらわれる, 目が合う), unless that noun is the doer's own body (手に入れる, 目にする, 身に付ける) or the row holds を; before 目に, 耳に, 気に rows the noun must be a person, a role or a pronoun (皇帝の目につく 황제의 눈에 띄는, 海の目に入る stays 바다가) ties the noun before it to that noun, 의 (土埃の波にさらわれた 흙먼지의 파도에 휩쓸렸다), and nothing after 내, 제, 네. が before まるで, 全然, まったく and the like and わからない is (을)를. An imperative quoted with という before a noun is -라는 (殲滅しろという意思 섬멸하라는 의사).

column3: A request (ください, 下さい, どうぞ, お願い) later in the sentence, before its 。, ！ or ？.
A gift (差し上げる, 進呈する, お渡しする) later in the sentence, before its 。, ！ or ？.
A 方 that is a person: its は, も or comma leads to a request, its に or には to a gift, or its が, は or も comes before an honoured being.
The Sino reading of a kanji digit and its digit.

Words of notices and public signs. A 方 after what a person does is a person, 분, and the word before it is honorific (-시는 분, -신 분, a verb's ない -지 않으시는 분), when its は, も or comma leads to a request in the same sentence, its に or には to a gift, or its が, は or も comes right before いらっしゃる, おられる or おります (参加される方は、受付までお越しください 참가하시는 분은, 접수까지 와 주세요, パスワードを忘れた方は 패스워드를 잊으신 분은); not after a verb of what happens to a thing (verb.thing-state: 割れた方は 깨진 편은), an の or が subject's する (音のする方), or an adjective unless it says a noun.own-condition (体調の悪い方 컨디션이 안 좋으신 분, 古い方 낡은 편); the comparison 方 stays (した方がいい 하는 것이 좋다) (GRM-3750). The 되다 of a verbal noun's される before a person 方 or noun.honored-person is the honorific 하시다, and the を it turned into (이)가 is (을)를 again (来店されるお客様 내점하시는 손님); with no を, a noun.chosen-passive is 되시다 (指名される方 지명되시는 분) and a noun.thing-passive stays (削除される方のデータ) (GRM-3751). のため after a noun.purpose-tame noun is (을)를 위해 (健康のため 건강을 위해), after a noun.cause-tame noun 때문에 (メンテナンスのため 유지보수 때문에), with a に right after it (을)를 위해, a one-word のために after a cause noun 때문에, 何のため before a comma 무엇을 위해, and after an ongoing 中 중이기 때문에 (GRM-3752). 同期 before する, or after the の of a noun.synced-data, is 동기화 (LEX-4630). A 家 after a particle is 집, not the house name 가 (貴族の家 귀족의 집), unless the の before it was dropped (LEX-4631). The 중 of a 中 after a person's dropped の is spaced (お客様の中に 손님 중에, お客様の中を 손님 중을) (LEX-4634). で after テスト, 試験 or 模試 before a noun.test-score is 에서, and 取る after one is 받다 (テストで赤点取る 테스트에서 낙제점 받는다) (LEX-4635). 方 after a person in 様, さま or 殿 is 들 (お客様方 손님들), and 先生方 is 선생님들 (LEX-4644). 必要とされる is 필요로 하다 after a person's に (as (이)가), 誰にも (누구도) or a を object, and before a person noun in the negative with no に before it (必要とされてない人間 필요로 하지 않는 인간); otherwise its negative is 필요하지 않다 (許可は必要とされていない 허가는 필요하지 않다) (LEX-4636). 配信 after the を or の of a noun.song is 공개 (新曲を配信する 신곡을 공개한다) (LEX-4639). 前倒しになる is 앞당겨지다 and 前倒しにする 앞당기다 (LEX-4633). 思い出す after the を of a thing is 떠올리다 (LEX-4638). うまい after a food noun's が, は, も or comma, past degree adverbs (word.degree-adverb), is 맛있다 (この料理はめっちゃうまい 이 요리는 엄청 맛있다), and one read 맛있다 after a food noun with が is 능숙하다 when a person is the は or も topic before it (彼女は料理がうまい 그녀는 요리가 능숙하다) (LEX-4645). 配信 before 開始, 日, 中 or 予定 in a clause whose topic is a noun.song is 공개 too (新曲は、配信開始 신곡은, 공개 개시) (LEX-4639). The でも of とでも思う that a か, のか or の of the clause asks with is dropped, and 思ってんの is 생각하는 거야 (気づかないとでも思ってんの？ 눈치채지 못한다고 생각하는 거야?) (GRM-3756). 困っている after a first-person subject, or ending a clause inside 「」 with no other subject, is 곤란하다, not 곤란해하다 (LEX-4646). エッチ read 섹스 is 변태 before ！, 。 or the end of what is said, unless after と or との, and 야한 것 before っぽい (LEX-4702). 仏 read 부처 right before a noun is 프랑스 (仏艦艇 프랑스 함정) (LEX-4703). The kana あつい read 뜨겁다 before or about a noun.thick-thing is 두껍다 (あつい本 두꺼운 책), and about a noun.hot-air 덥다 (今日はあつい 오늘은 덥다) (LEX-4701). 全く or まったく opening a line before a comma, an ellipsis or a cry is 정말이지, ちょっと doubled is 잠깐, なんだって before できる, する or やれる is 뭐든지, and 殿 read 전 opening a line or after a comma or a cry, not in 殿を務める, is 주군 (LEX-4706). 付き合う after に, まで, ちょっと or とことん with no と and a person before it is 함께하다; 送る after まで with no を object that is not a person is 배웅하다, and 送ってくる with no person object 보내 오다; 手を打つ after それで or これで is 합의하다, いただく with a food object in ます or ましょう 먹다, and 言いつける to a person 고자질하다 (LEX-4707). A kanji digit next to 〇 is a place value and is written as the digit (一三〇〇 1300) (LEX-4709). The blank い of ていた that gave its 것 to the verb before it keeps no ending (言っていたのを 말한 것을) (GRM-3754).

column3: The 하다 adjective of a Korean adverb of manner in 하게 or 히 (촉촉하게 촉촉한, 단호히 단호한).

A mimetic word or an adverb of manner with the した or している of する right before a noun it describes says what the noun is like, not what was done: the Korean adjective of that word (しっかりとした造り 제대로 된 구조, ちゃんとした服 제대로 된 옷, はっきりとした声 뚜렷한 목소리, のんびりとした口調 느긋한 말투, ぐったりとした様子 축 늘어진 모습), by the noun's class sometimes another one (しっかりした子 착실한 아이, しっかりとした体格 다부진 체격, ほっそりとした指 가느다란 손가락, あっさりした返事 간단한 대답). A word in り or と read as an adverb in 하게 or 히 takes the 하다 adjective of that adverb before した (しっとりとした肌 촉촉한 피부, きっぱりとした口調 단호한 어조), and a root the sound stage writes for a mimetic takes its adjective before している too (ふんわりしている髪 폭신한 머리카락). The same holds before the もの that a した carries as 것 (あっさりしたものだった 담백한 것이었다) and for a と read apart before する (ふんわりとした髪). Not before a formal noun or one of time or result (noun.act-head: ちゃんとしたことがない 제대로 한 적이 없다) or a final particle, after an object in を earlier in its clause (掃除をすぐにちゃんとした人) or a place in で right before it (リビングでのんびりしている), before したい, a comma, the end or the 것 of らしい, ようだ and みたい (ちゃんとしたらしい 제대로 한 것 같다), nor in the past of している.

column3: What ends the search from a condition to its main clause: a quote (a verb that took its と, not the こと of a verb: 付き合う事ぐらいは出来た), a sentence end, or a clause that ends in a comma and no condition.

A ば or たら condition read (으)면 before a main clause in the past is one that did not hold, (았)더라면: a condition of ている or of ない (an adjective or いない, not the copula でなければ) in ば before a sentence that ends in the past (降っていなければ 오지 않았더라면, 君がいなければ 네가 없었더라면), and any ば or たら before a sentence that ends in a past with のに, かもしれない, だろう or はず (来れば間に合ったのに 왔더라면, 違っていたら刺さっていたかもしれない), unless the condition is one of seeing, saying or thinking (傍から見れば). A verb negated in ば (来なければ) takes it only before a sentence that ends in a past negative, a past of いい or such a supposition (来なければ乗ることもなかった 오지 않았더라면), not before a plain past of what followed (開けなければ並んだ). A quote (と, って), a clause that ends in a comma and no condition, or the end of the sentence stops the search, so a condition inside what is thought keeps (으)면; so do an obligation (なければならない) and a condition after と (としたら) or before a list in も (もいなければ).

column3: A filler typed between a word and the word it goes with: laughter (ｗｗ, 草, (笑)), an ellipsis or a long or wave mark.
An adjective, an adjectival noun or an adverb.
An adjective or an adjectival noun that ends the utterance (かわいい, かわいいｗ), not one that goes on (危ないから), quotes or asks (アンフェアって？), nor one after a space, which parts it like a comma (ちょ　うるさい).

The ちょ that opens an utterance, read 잠깐 by the sound stage before a pause, a space or laughter (ちょｗｗ待って 잠깐ㅋㅋ 기다려), is the intensifier 超, 완전, when the next word past fillers (filler-item) is an adjective or an adjectival noun that ends the utterance (ちょｗｗかわいい 완전ㅋㅋ 귀여워, ちょ…かわいい 완전… 귀여워); a comma, a space, another word or a predicate that goes on keeps the interjection (ちょ、かわいい 잠깐, 귀여워, ちょ　うるさい 잠깐 시끄러워, ちょ… 危ないから 잠깐… 위험하니까). The kana ちょう that opens a phrase (at the start, after a particle, a space or a comma) is that intensifier before an adjective, an adjectival noun or an adverb (ちょうかわいい 완전 귀여워), not inside a word (どんちょう) and not the insect elsewhere.

The よ that ends a line right after the dictionary form of a verb of verb.warning-act (怒る, 殴る, 撃つ, 燃やす), or of an action verb after a warning adverb (本気で, 本当に, マジで, 絶対), read as the plain 해, is a warning aimed at the listener, -ㄹ 거야 (本気で怒るよ 정말로 화낼 거야, 殴るよ 때릴 거야); after a verb of verb.announce-move (帰る, 寝る, 行く) it announces the speaker's own move, -ㄹ게 (先に帰るよ 먼저 돌아갈게, もう寝るよ 이제 잘게), but not a call to a group (みんな、行くよ！); before ？ with no question word in the sentence it is the warning asked back, -ㄴ다? (怒るよ？ 화낸다?). Other verbs keep 해: a state, a feeling or what happens (感じるよ 느껴, 心が軽くなるよ 가벼워져, 夕日が落ちるよ 떨어져), and a real question (どうするよ？; spec GRM-3940).

column3: A plain polite question ますか that ends the sentence, after a verb of doing with no question word before it, offers or proposes the act only on a positive sign: a confirm-dialog action (word.confirm-action: 上書きしますか？ 덮어쓰기할까요?, 回復薬を使いますか), a choice with にする (お風呂にしますか 목욕으로 할까요), asking what to do (どうしますか, いかがいたしますか), or a cue of an offer before it in the sentence (word.offer-cue: さて、帰りますか 자, 돌아갈까요; お茶でも飲みますか): 까요. A plain question with none of them (日本語を話しますか) keeps 합니까. A system message in 『』 or 《》, or a prompt with と, 》 or the answers after it, asks the reader's will: 시겠습니까 (『チュートリアルを行いますか？』 튜토리얼을 실시하시겠습니까?), and so does a question after an honorific verb, される read as respectful included: 겠습니까 (お休みになりますか 쉬시겠습니까, ご確認されますか 확인하시겠습니까). Not after a verb that states, knows or can (思いますか, ありますか, できますか), after 来る (そう来ますか), before an exclamation mark, after ている, される not read as respectful, くれる, a passive, potential or causative, nor in a sentence that asks about someone named with は, が or a second-person pronoun, or about a habit (adverb.habit: 毎日勉強しますか).

act-scope with no scolding interjection before the word (scold-before) and no exclamation mark after it (reproach-mark): what an invitation asks.

A negative question that ends the sentence after a verb one does on purpose (no :invite-state) invites the listener or asks them for the act (spec MNG-7): the casual ない？ and ないか？ is 지 않을래 (カフェ行かない？ 카페 가지 않을래?, 食べないか？ 먹지 않을래?), the polite ませんか is 지 않을래요 (一緒に行きませんか？ 함께 가지 않을래요?), and 합쇼 지 않겠습니까 with -시- after a keigo verb: a respectful one (verb.respectful, お〜になる, ていただける), whose Korean has its 시 already (ご覧になりませんか 보시지 않겠습니까), or a humble one with no first person but a genitive before it in its sentence (verb.humble-invite: 参りませんか 가시지 않겠습니까; 私も参りませんか keeps 저도 가지 않을래요), and the request てくれないか is 주지 않겠어 (妻になってくれないか？ 아내가 되어 주지 않겠어?). A real question keeps its negative: a state, knowing or ability (知らない？, いない？, 思わない？, できませんか), ている (増えてない？), a question word, a subject in は or が (田中は行かない？), まだ or 全然, の or ん before the mark (寝ないの？), and an exclamation (行かないか！).

column3: Words and particles of narration and dialogue whose reading depends on a neighbour. に between 挨拶 and a verb of going or coming is the purpose 하러 (ご挨拶に参ります 인사하러 가겠습니다); 転倒 and 横恋慕 before する are the verbs 넘어지다 and 남의 짝을 넘보다; 一筋 right after a noun is 외길 (仕事一筋 일 외길), not after a thread, a hair or light, nor before も or ほど; 付き添う after a person and に is 동행하다 with 와/과 (父に付き添い 아버지와 동행해), not before もらう or いただく; 付き合う after に, には or にも with no と in the clause is 어울리다, not 사귀다, unless it describes a partner (付き合っている彼氏); 命 after a person and の before 受ける is the order 명; あまりの before 変わりよう is 너무나; 返す with no object, after a way of answering (笑顔で, あわてて, うなずいて) or a quote, is 대답하다; 御機嫌よう that closes a quoted speech after another sentence that takes leave (word.leave-taking), or follows では or それでは, is the farewell 안녕히 계세요; ない of existence after よほど in the same clause is 있지 않다 (よほど実家の権力がない限り 상당히 본가의 권력이 있지 않는 한); ぞ after a state (ある, いる, ている, 思う, 気がする) is the plain 해체 -어, not the will -겠어 (聞いているぞ 듣고 있어); the degree ending ほど before a verb or an adjective is 정도로 (ないほど美しい 없을 정도로 아름다운), not before a copula; 挙げ句 opening a clause is 급기야, and に after a verb ending read 끝에 is dropped; やってくる after を is 해 오다 (ゲームをやってきた 게임을 해 왔다); 頃に改めて is 무렵에 다시; なんて and なんだって standing alone before a question mark are 뭐라고 (뭐래 after は), and だって after a noun before a question mark is the echo (이)라고; でなければ after a comma is 그렇지 않으면; かわってくれる is 대신해 주다; Nはなりません is 안됩니다; になど before なる is 따위가; 手はない after a verb is -ㄹ 수는 없다; やる after をもって, を懸けて or を込めて is 하다; 迷惑な before ど or んて, んか is 민폐 같은 건; 今までで and これまでで before a superlative (一番, 最高) are 지금까지 중에서; の after 入り read 넣은 is dropped; なんでもない before 顔 is 아무렇지도 않은; おやすみなさ cut off before its い is 안녕히 주무세; the honorific copula 이시다 (であられる, でいらっしゃる) before a noun is 이신, not 이시는; 正直に before a verb of saying is 솔직하게; だいたい opening an utterance before a comma is 애초에, unless what follows is a rough amount (こんな, そう, 形, a number, くらい) or 分かる; ちょっとした before こと is 사소한; に控える after a room or a spot beside someone is 에서 대기하다; 婚活 named as an abbreviation (略して婚活, 通称婚活, 婚活と略す) is 혼활, elsewhere 결혼 활동; に before 버금가다 is 에; なんで after a space that parts it from the word before is 왜, not the reason 이니까 (アモル なんで 아모르 왜).

column3: The し that ends an utterance in quotation marks, also before ね, さ or な, gives a reason and ends the sentence, so it is not the connective 고: the speaker's reason is -거든 (別に怒ってないし 별로 화내지 않거든), and with a も in its clause before an affirmative predicate it is a reason the listener can see, -잖아 (星も綺麗だし 별도 예쁘잖아). だろうし and はずだし are -ㄹ 테니까 (-ㄹ 테고 with more after them), わけだし -는 거잖아; -잖아 needs a cue that the reason is evident (shi-shared). A し with more of the sentence after it stays 고 (暑いし、疲れたし、 덥고, 지쳤고,).

column3: The の read 의 after ご and a verbal noun, before a person a host speaks to (noun.honored-person), makes the verbal noun the honored person's act: 하신 (ご予約のお客様 예약하신 손님), or 하시는 for an ongoing act (noun.honorific-ongoing: ご利用のお客様 이용하시는 손님), and the 方 after it is 분. A 方 read 편 right after an honorific attributive in 시는 or 신 is 분 (ご希望の方 희망하시는 분). A 方 with no particle of a person after it (は, が, に, へ, も, の, で) is ほう, the matter asked for, and stays (ご確認の方をお願いします). When の, 方 and the particle after it are one word (の方は), the verbal noun takes 하신 분 or 하시는 분 and that word keeps the particle that can follow 분 (ご来店の方は 내점하신 분은, ご参加の方に 참가하신 분에게), unless a noun and の before ご make the verbal noun a thing (メニューのご注文の方は 메뉴 주문은).

column3: The humble 参る and まいる of the speaker. Its present ます that ends a sentence goes: 가겠습니다 (白雲、参ります！ 백운, 가겠습니다!); its past comes to where the listener is: 왔습니다 (スウェーデンから参りました 스웨덴에서 왔습니다); its ましょう goes along: 갑시다. After a て form the present goes on doing it, 어 가겠습니다 (徹底してまいります 철저히 해 가겠습니다), but after an errand of verb.errand it is going to do it and coming back, 어 오겠습니다 (お茶を淹れてまいります 차를 끓여 오겠습니다).

column3: An active おいで command that closes its utterance.

The おいで of a て form is a command to come after a return or accompanying verb, to keep waiting, silent or in a posture after ko-verb.oide-stay, and otherwise to go and do it and come back. A copula attached to おいで instead closes a respectful progressive, 고 계시다 or 어 계시다 for a result state. Standalone おいで and おいでになる are separate.

column3: The word before is a pronoun of the listener, alone or with a plural suffix (お前, 貴公ら).
A recipient in に before the word in its clause that is the listener (お前に, 貴公らに).
A に before the word in its clause after anything but a pronoun of the listener (みんなに, 彼女に).
The speaker as subject or topic before the word in its clause (私が, 俺は).
A word of word.inclusive before the word in its sentence, up to the verb before (一緒に, われらの).

The volitional read 자 of a verb of giving to someone (verb.grant: 授ける, 与える, 教える, 見せる, 許す, and あげる read 주다) that ends the sentence, not after a て form, with the listener in に (pronoun.listener), the speaker as subject, or an object in its clause in speech (before a closing bracket or an exclamation mark), and no other recipient in に and no word of word.inclusive in its sentence, is the speaker's will to the listener, not an invitation: 주마, the verb in 어 with 주마 when its Korean is not 주다 already (力を授けよう 힘을 내려 주마, いいことを教えよう 좋은 것을 가르쳐 주마, 私が許そう 내가 용서해 주마). Not before a question mark, nor みんなに見せよう or われらの力を見せよう, which invite.

column3: A verb of storing or putting away (verb.store) before the word in its sentence, not an auxiliary after a て form.
A container (noun.container) in から before the word in its clause.

A 出す read 내다 takes a thing out, 꺼내다, after a container in から in its clause (ポケットから財布を出した 포켓에서 지갑을 꺼냈다), or with no object in its clause after a verb of storing or putting away (verb.store) in its sentence (収納し、出してみる). Right after that verb in its 連用 or て form and a comma the store is undone: the verb takes 었다가 and the comma goes (収納し、出してみる 수납했다가 꺼내 본다). 声を出す, 手を出す and 元気を出す keep 내다.

column3: The もう before a number with a counter of counter.added (in one word or two), with a verb, an adjective, a word of word.give-request, a pause or the end after the count, adds that many: the count, then 더 (もう一匹いた 한 마리 더 있었다, もう１錠飲む 1정 더 마신다); もう一人 has its own row. Before は, が, の or a noun, one more of them is another one, 또 (もう一つの 또 하나의, もう一枚は 또 한 장은). It keeps もう after the count before another particle, a copula or する (もう一泊する), before a noun after a count of more than one, before a past verb after a count of more than one (もう二人来た 벌써 두 사람 왔다), and with counters of a time, an age or an order (もう三年経った 벌써 3년 지났다); もう一日 or もう1日 right before a verb that is no passing of time (経つ, 過ぎる, 終わる, ある) is one more day, 하루 더 (もう一日待てば 하루 더 기다리면).

column3: A って read as the topic (은)는 that ends a sentence right after a predicate quotes it: after a plain ending in 다 it is 고 (楽しかったって 즐거웠다고), after a polite one the plain form with 고요 (やりますって 한다고요, 起きてますって 일어나고 있다고요), after a question in 가 that is no explanatory のか, 냐고 (眠いかって？ 졸리냐고?), after a wondering 까 the direct quote 하고, and after なさい the order 라고. ってば read (은)는 정말 there insists: 다니까, 다니까요, 라니까, and after the copula だ (이)라니까 (冗談だってば 농담이라니까); not after the explanatory ん or の. Before a question mark, after a 해체 ending (어, 야, 지, 까) it is 라고 (何してるかって？ 뭐하고 있어라고?).

column3: A とは after a noun read (이)란 or (와)과는 that ends the sentence, or stands before a closing ね or な, wonders at what it names: (이)라니 (まさかお前とはね 설마 너라니); after a verb its 다고는 is 다니 there (負けるとはね 지다니). A とは read (이)란 with a word of word.toha-partner or word.comitative later in its clause (before a comma, a sentence end or the first other verb) names the partner of a comparison or a relationship: (와)과는 (それとは違う 그것과는 다르다, お前とは長い付き合いだ 너와는 긴 교제다). A どうなる after its own subject in が is no partner word (人生とはなにがどうなるかわからないものだ 인생이란) unless a person, a pronoun or a name stands before the とは (彼とは何がどうなったの 그와는). After a person, a pronoun or a name, with a verb other than the copula later in its sentence, the とは is that partner too, (와)과는, unless a word of word.toha-define (何, どんな, 一体, 誰) or a pause follows it, which asks what or who it is (メイドとは一体何 메이드란 도대체 뭐).

column3: The comma is a pause before a particle, の, the copula or みたい that still belong to the predicate before it (嬉しい、です), not before a conjunction of word.clause-start (でも).

After the comma a new clause starts: a demonstrative adverb or conjunction of word.clause-start (そう思った, でも), a demonstrative pronoun of word.clause-pronoun with が, は, も or を (それが), a conjunction or an interjection, or a predicate that ends its clause right there, before a mark, the end or a particle that joins clauses, and holds no subject of its own (転がる、転がる。, 汚い、弱いからだ).

A bare attributive verb or adjective (the present 0 of a verb, the past 8 of a verb, the 4 of an adjective in い) right before a comma ends its clause when a new clause starts after the comma (comma-clause): the terminal form 다 (わからない、それが人生だ 모른다, 그것이 인생이다, よくわからない、でも行く 잘 모른다, 하지만 간다). Before a noun phrase it describes, even one with は or も (映画館の中で食べた、ポップコーンは 먹은, 팝콘은), it stays attributive (ドアの内側に設置された、鈴の音 설치된, 방울 소리), and so before a particle, の or the copula after a pausing comma (嬉しい、です).

column3: The ように follows the ている of a verb (殴られているように, 泣いてるように).
The first predicate after the word in its sentence asks, tells, wishes, tries or makes (verb.youni-purpose): the ように says what is aimed at.

A ように of a verb read 도록 or 게 is a likeness, not an aim: 것처럼 before a verb of seeming (verb.youni-seem: 泣いているように見えた 울고 있는 것처럼 보였다, 騙そうとしているようには見えなかった 속이려 하고 있는 것처럼은 보이지 않았다), 것처럼 after ている when the first predicate after it does not ask, tell, wish, try or make (殴られているように頭が痛む 맞고 있는 것처럼 머리가 아프다; 待っているように言った keeps 도록), and 듯이 after まるで or あたかも in its sentence (まるで許しを請い跪くように 마치 용서를 빌며 무릎 꿇듯이) or when the first predicate after it is a gesture, a look, a voice or a touch (verb.youni-depicted) and the verb before it is one a person does: not a potential, a passive, a verb of what happens (verb.youni-unwilled) or 있다, 되다, 받다, with no が subject or なるべく before it (からかうように笑った 놀리듯이 웃었다; 目線を合わせるようにしゃがむ keeps 도록). After a noun, かのように and かのような are 인 것처럼 and 인 것 같은 (子供かのように 아이인 것처럼).

column3: The ほしい (欲しい) of a wish.

The verb before is a て form that the rules read as 기를 or 면 for ほしい, not the blank ある of であって nor a main ある or いる of a state (こうあってほしい 이랬으면 좋겠다), which no one does for the speaker; the auxiliary of ている is (待っていてほしい 기다리고 있어 줬으면 한다).

The ほしい after a て form wishes someone did something: 아 줬으면 좋겠다 (早く来てほしい 빨리 와 줬으면 좋겠다, 教えてほしいのだけれど 가르쳐 줬으면 좋겠는데), 주었으면 좋겠다 after a verb that already gives (てくれて), not 기를 원하다 or 면 좋겠다; it keeps 하다 where it describes a noun or is past (見てほしいもの 봐 줬으면 하는 것, 来てほしかった 와 줬으면 했다). column3: The など opens a line or follows a sentence end or a pause.

A など that opens a line or follows a sentence end or a pause, right before a quoting と, takes up what was said before it, not a list: its と is 하고 where the word stage read it as the companion (와)과, and the など adds nothing (察しろっての！などと、内心でボヤく 눈치채라고! 하고, 속으로 투덜대다). After anything but a noun (a closing bracket, a predicate), before a verb of thinking or saying, など+と reads the same way (「嘘だ」などと叫んだ 「거짓말이다」 하고 외쳤다); before と言 it is 같은 말을, keeping the voice (「嘘だ」などと言った 「거짓말이다」 같은 말을 했다). After a list of nouns など keeps its 등 (りんごやみかんなどと言った 사과나 귤 등이라고 말했다).

column4: A など, なんか or なんて right after a single noun (no listing before it in its noun phrase, no particle after it) belittles the noun when its clause ends in a predicate that says no or brushes the noun aside (spec LEX-90, LEX-91); a negative inside a clause that goes on (食べない人, しないと, しないように, 起きないこと) or in a question is no such end. Before a rhetorical refusal (ものか, もんか) all three are 따위 (言葉なんか信じるものか 말 따위 믿을까 보냐). A など is 같은 건 before a predicate that says the noun is not there or cannot be (余地などない 여지 같은 건 없다, 理由など見つかるはずもない 이유 같은 건 발견될 리도 없다), 같은 건 in narration and before a passive or respectful predicate (予算など議論されなかった 예산 같은 건 논의되지 않았다), and 따위 before any other that says no (言葉など信じない 말 따위 믿지 않는다), not the listing 등. column3: Words and clause shapes the web examples misread. The kana さして read 별로 with no negative after it is the verb 差す: 쓰고 after an umbrella with を, 넣고 after 目薬を, 차고 after 腰に, 비쳐 after light with が, 쓰고 alone before 帰る or 行く (spec LEX-4560). 歳で after an adnominal or の is 나이에, not 세에 (LEX-4561); 自信 is 자신감 unless 있다 or 없다 follows (LEX-4562); the noun 恐れ is 두려움 unless a verb's clause names the danger (LEX-4563); 暫くは is 한동안은 (LEX-4567); 意見する is 의견을 말하다 (LEX-4570); 貧乏 right before a noun is 가난한 (LEX-4571); N切れ before そう is N 직전 (LEX-4572); 持ちかける with talk or a request is 꺼내다 or 제안하다 (LEX-4573); 時の before a person after a conjunction is 당대의 (LEX-4574); それに before 気付く is 그것을 알아차리다, Nに … 気付く with only an adverb between is N(을)를 알아차리다, and それに before the verb 答える is 거기에, as before 応える (LEX-4575); そう言わずに before a request is 그러지 말고 (LEX-4577). より after a place or time noun before a comparison is 보다 (GRM-3700); a count with きり before a verb is 만 (GRM-3701); なんて before もの does not say 같은 건 twice (GRM-3702); a na-adjective's なの right before a verb is 것 (GRM-3703); 何の or 一切の … なく before a comma is 없이 (GRM-3704); a quoted だろう before ！ that opens its quote or goes on is 잖아 (GRM-3705); a person's の before a verb of a quality is 의 (GRM-3706); なさい after polite speech in its quote is 주세요 (GRM-3707); a verb stem with でもする is -기라도 하다 (GRM-3708); a past of hunger in speech is the present (GRM-3709); ておいて going on into its clause is 놓고 and 置いて 두고 (GRM-3710); もいれば, もあれば before another も … ある lists, 있고 (GRM-3711); こともあり、 gives a reason, 것도 있어서 (GRM-3712).

column3: 必ずしも stands before the word in its sentence with no other word that says no between.

column3: 一緒 as a predicate that says two things are the same is 마찬가지, not 함께: after と with a nominalized clause, a demonstrative or a time before it (食べるのと一緒 먹는 것과 마찬가지, それと一緒 그것과 마찬가지, 昔と一緒 옛날과 마찬가지), after a て form with も or after どれも, どっちも (何をやっても一緒 뭘 해도 마찬가지), after は, が or も with a noun of noun.same-attribute (結果は一緒 결과는 마찬가지), and standing as an answer after an agreeing word and a comma (そうそう、一緒。 맞아 맞아, 똑같아). column3: A てやる read 주다 after a verb of verb.harming with no に before that verb is a threat, not a favour: in quotation marks it is 버릴 거야 and 주니까 is 버릴 테니까 (「殺してやる」 죽여 버릴 거야, ぶん殴ってやるからな 후려쳐 버릴 테니까), and the plain 준다 outside them is the will of the verb itself, 겠다 (殴ってやる。 때리겠다); the verb itself takes that ending where its Korean already ends in 버리다 (ぶっ飛ばしてやる 날려 버릴 거야) and for 겠다. After a causative of verb.harming-causative or 後悔させる the threat is 겠다, which the speech level of a quoted line makes 겠어 (思い知らせてやる 깨닫게 하겠다, 後悔させてやる 후회시키겠어).
The や of a てやる read 주다 after a conjugating word.
The verb before it is a verb of harm in its て form with no に right before it.
The ending is the casual 줄게, or the plain 준다 inside quotation marks, which the speech level of the line turns casual.

column3: A quotation in って fused into the ending of a predicate, read with the quoting 다고, 라고, 냐고 or 자고, right before a noun of noun.quoted-clause that it describes takes the adnominal quote: its 고 is 는 (ハンドラーになったって話 핸들러가 됐다는 이야기, 生きてるって感じだ 살아 있다는 느낌이다), and a こと or 事 after it is the bound noun 것 (投票しろってことか 투표하라는 것인가). Not a たって or だって after a question word, which is concessive (誰がどう考えたって評判が 누가 어떻게 생각해도); the noun goes on as a noun: not before する (来いって電話した 오라고 전화했다) or an adjective (走るって気持ちいい). A past たって or だって read as the concession 어도 before such a noun is the same quotation in the past, 었다는 (見られていたって事 보여지고 있었다는 것, 病に掛かったって報せ 병에 걸렸다는 소식), unless a question word before it, 意味, 話 before に or が, or a noun with は or も, the topic of the next clause (走ったって気分は晴れない 달려도 기분은), make it a concession (いくら言ったって意味がない 아무리 말해도 의미가 없다).
The word after it is a noun a quotation describes, going on as a noun.

column3: A だって or たって that goes on to a verb of saying, thinking or knowing in its clause is the quote 라고, 다고 (spec GRM-3920): a noun's だって after a subject は or が in the clause (田中斗真が犯人だって告げてる 범인이라고, 守りたいのは紗奈だって気付いた 사나라고), and the past たって of a verb before such a verb (答えを見つけたって伝えておく 찾아냈다고). Without the subject a noun's だって is 도 (私だってそう思う 저도) unless it is no person and a verb of saying comes (出来高制だって最初に言った 성과급제라고).

A verb of saying, telling (話す), thinking, noticing or knowing ahead in the clause, a verb of verb.quote-start, or its noun before する (説明してくれた), and not a noun spelled like one (答えは), or a noun of verb.quote-stem (勘違いして), not in a condition (言ってみれば) nor 聞く (いくら言ったって聞かない 말해도).
A subject は or が before the word in its clause, also one a predicate's ending holds (守りたいのは).

column3: A noun's だって before a predicate is the 도 of "X too, even X" (今朝だって無垢な赤子のように 오늘 아침도, 声色だって違ってる 음색도); (이)라도 stays before a prohibition (女だって触っちゃダメだ 여자라도), after an indefinite or a concessive adverb (何度, どっち, どんな人, いくら鉄砲だって), before a condition (20ドルだって取れたら), before いい or 構わない (何だっていい), and for the least able before an ability (子供だって分かる 애라도). Before a verb of thinking or knowing, a noun that is no person or time, or a person of noun.relation-person, is quoted, (이)라고 (限界だって思う 한계라고, 友達だって思ってた 친구라고; spec GRM-3923). A time of noun.time-ni takes 에도 (夜だって働く 밤에도), weather of noun.weather-come before an act is (이)가 와도 (雨だって行く 비가 와도 간다), and a noun before 明かす is quoted, (이)라고, or before 分かる with an adjective on it (이)라는 걸 (すごい人だって分かる).

column3: A word of degree or count (どれだけ, どれほど, どんなに, いかに, 何度, なんと) before the word in its sentence.
The next word is a か that ends its sentence or quote, or a comma or a pause follows it.

A ことか (こと, 事) that ends a sentence after a word of degree or count (どれだけ, どれほど, どんなに, いかに, 何度, なんと) does not ask; it exclaims how much (spec GRM-145): a past verb takes -었던가 (何度言ったことか 몇 번 말했던가), a present verb -는가 (どれほど軽くなることか 얼마나 가벼워지는가), a copula 인가, an adjective -(으)ㄴ가 (なんと美しいことか 얼마나 아름다운가), not 건가 or 일인가; before 分からない a past verb takes -었는지 (何度思ったことか分からない 몇 번 생각했는지 모른다); どんなに and なんと before it are 얼마나, not 아무리, 무려 or 너무나. A ことか before を, と or another verb, ものか, and a verb right after なんと (なんとしたことか, なんと切り出したものか) stay.

column3: さえ between a て form and the auxiliary of a condition (知ってさえいれば, 退いてさえくれれば) says that one thing is enough (spec GRM-150): the verb takes -기만 하면, with いる dropped (知ってさえいれば 알기만 하면) but kept after a verb of verb.result-state (生きてさえいれば 살아 있기만 하면), する dropped (生きてさえすれば 살기만 하면), しまう read 버리다 and any other auxiliary kept (バレてさえしまえば 들켜 버리기만 하면, 退いてさえくれれば 물러나 주기만 하면); with a negative いない in ば it is -지만 않으면 (服装をしてさえいなければ 복장을 하지만 않으면), and a negative that ends the clause -지도 않다 (気付いてさえいなかった 깨닫지도 않았다); a noun in 기 before さえしなければ takes 만 (捨てさえしなければ 버리기만 하지 않으면); never 조차 between the two.

column3: A verb that takes from where one starts, flees or comes (始める, 逃げる, 離れる, 来る) later in the sentence.

A ことから with a comma after it, after a predicate, gives the ground of what follows, why something is named, held or known (spec GRM-151): -다는 점에서 (人畜無害な魔物であることから、 인축무해한 마물이라는 점에서, 回復力が高いことから、 회복력이 높다는 점에서, 驚いていないことから、 놀라지 않는다는 점에서), このことから、 이 점에서, そのことから、 그 점에서, not 것으로부터. column3: A question word asks the word: the word starts with it (どうする), or it stands before the word in its clause, alone or starting a て form (何やって), with no comma, no も (何の知識もない, どのクラブも, 何の苦も無く), no question closed by か (何を聞かれたかは, 泣いているのかと), no quotation in と or って but one that the verb of saying or thinking after it takes (誰のせいだと思ってやがる), no concessive (何をしても, 何をしたところで, 何を言ったって, どうあろうと) and no other predicate between them but a て form or a condition (どこを狙っている, どうすればいい).
The word ends its sentence with 。, a closing bracket or the end of the text, not with ！ or ？.

column4: A plain predicate that ends a sentence after a question word, with no か, asks. With のだ or んだ in speech whose level is 해체 it is the 해체 question -는 거야 (何やっているんだ、おまえ 뭐 하고 있는 거야, 너; なにが悪いんだ 뭐가 나쁜 거야), and outside quotes a bare verb before 。, or at the end of a sentence of narration, asks with -나 (人夫、何人動員した。 인부, 몇 사람 동원했나.; なぜ逃げる。 왜 도망치나.), not the -다 of a statement; inside quotes the speech-level stage gives the bare verb the end of its level (どこを狙っている 어디를 노리고 있어). Not the exclamation 何と before a word that is no verb (何と美しいんだ), nor after a concessive (何をしても無駄なんだ 뭘 해도 쓸데없다), nor before ！ or ？, whose ends the compose stage writes (spec SPC-1).

column3: A verb whose Korean the particle or the word before it decides, where the sense table cannot see the particle: 離れる after を is leaving that place, 떠나다 (学園を離れた日 학원을 떠난 날); 触れる after a hand or a finger and を is putting it on, 대다 (両手を触れて 양손을 대고); 向く after a weapon or a gaze in が and a noun in に is turning to it, 향하다, not being suited (得物が敵に向く 무기가 적에게 향한다); に当たる after a duty is taking it on, 임하다 (警備に当たる 경비에 임하다); 伺う after a greeting or a visit in に or a home in に is visiting, 찾아뵙다, and the greeting takes 하러 (挨拶に伺った 인사하러 찾아뵌); 伺う after a secret way of watching (こっそり, そっと) is the 窺う of watching, 엿보다; 注ぐ with an object in を before it is pouring, 붓다, not flowing in (血を、杯の中に注げ 피를, 잔 안에 부어라); 突っ伏す after 顔を is burying the face, 파묻다; the に after 相手 before できる is the object (を) of 상대를 하다 (相手に出来るか 상대를 할 수 있을지), not before できるだけ nor when 相手 itself follows を or も (全軍を相手に出来る keeps 상대로); 押し付ける with a fist, a face or a body earlier in its clause, past the three words the sense table sees, is pressing, 누르다 (拳を心臓の位置へと押し付けた 주먹을 심장 위치로 눌렀다).

column3: A だろうが, or a でしょうが before an exclamation mark or after ん (a polite でしょうが may still concede: できないでしょうが。).
An adverb of supposition or musing (まぁ, たぶん, おそらく, きっと) stands before the word in its sentence: the supposition concedes.

A だろうが, でしょうが (だろが, でしょが) that ends an utterance inside a quote is no concession but a retort that the hearer should know it: -잖아, in でしょうが -잖아요, after a noun (이)잖아 (仕方ないだろうが！ 어쩔 수 없잖아!, あなたが原因を作ったんでしょうが！！ 당신이 원인을 만들었잖아요!!, ほんの数分のことだろうが 그저 몇 분의 일이잖아), not 겠지만 or 겠지요가. Not in narration, where a final だろうが may concede (あるのだろうが。 있겠지만.), nor after another だろうが in its sentence (pairs: GRM-75).
The word is in a quote, with no earlier だろうが in its sentence, not after の (のだろうが concedes) and not after an adverb of musing.
The same for a supposition before a separate が.

column3: Misreadings fresh news, web novel and game lines showed. The old copula じゃ and the western や before から are だから, (이)니까 (無駄じゃからな 쓸데없으니까, 予備分やから 예비분이니까), not the topic 은 and 매운 or 이나로부터. といい after a closing bracket or after a name given with 名を or 名前は, with no other といい in its sentence, quotes or names, (이)라며, (이)라고 하며, not the listing 도 그렇고. Hearsay そう after a closing quote is 라고 하다, after a contracted ている or ていた -고 있다고 하다, not 그렇다. A verbal noun of noun.intransitive-doeda after a subject of noun.event-subject (an operation, a plan, an event, a thing made or a record), with no object in its clause, in a plain statement (た, る, ます, ました, ている, ていない; no request, suggestion, prohibition, permission, condition or question), takes 되다 (サービスは終了した 서비스는 종료되었다). N人の国 before 籍 is N명의 국적, なのが before わかる is 인 것을. ことしかできない is (으)ㄹ 수밖에 없다, a past before のである that the word stage read 때문에 있다 is (으)ㄴ 것이다, a past before であろう is -었을. 続く after へ, or after に and a place before a noun, is a way that leads there, (으)로 이어지다. A ませんでしたね or ませんでしたよね after a word whose negative is 모르다 (Ma) is -었군요, not 모르지 않았군요. A してい read 하지 않다 (結婚, 注文: the negative is in the word) takes the past of a plain ending in place of a second negative: 결혼하지 않았습니까, not 결혼하지 않지 않습니까.

Not after こと or ため, after a question word (どんな展開にもなる), in a pair AにもBにも, nor before a negative, a potential, a condition or an auxiliary.

A word of word.evaluative-talk before こと, and a particle or nothing, and 言う, 抜かす or ほざく judges what is said: こと is 소리 (堅いことは言うな 딱딱한 소리는 하지 마, 馬鹿なことを言うな 바보같은 소리를 하지 마); 舐めた there is 얕보는, ふざけた 웃기는 and 甘い 안이한 (舐めたことを言うな 얕보는 소리를 하지 마, ふざけたことを抜かすな 웃기는 소리를 지껄이지 마). 舐めた before 真似 is 얕보는 짓 (舐めた真似をしやがって 얕보는 짓을 하다니). Before a word of a rule (武器にしちゃいけない 무기로 하면 안 된다, 人のせいにしちゃダメ), as しちゃう (本気にしちゃう) and at the end of the sentence (乱暴にしちゃ) it stays.

column3: A subject in が or a person in は before the word that is not the speaker (彼は来るから, バスが来るから).

The から after the dictionary form of an act one promises (verb.promise-act: 戻る, 返す, 払う, 待つ; a noun of noun.promise-act with する: 連絡する, 説明する), with no other subject before it in the sentence and a request or an order after it (promise-ask), gives the promise that the request leans on: -ㄹ 테니까 (すぐ戻るから、ここで待ってて 바로 돌아올 테니까, 여기서 기다리고 있어; お金は返すから、少しだけ貸して 돈은 갚을 테니까; spec LEX-4766). A state (降ってる, ある), a past (疲れたから), a negative or another subject (彼は来ないから) keeps 니까.

column3: A word before 言ってくれるな that makes it a prohibition (そんなこと, それを, 簡単に, 二度と, もう): without one 言ってくれるな is the exclamation at what was said (うれしいこと言ってくれるな 기쁜 말 해 주는구나).

The くれ of a request after a て form before a comma, which the word stage reads as the joining 주어 (黙っておくれ、もう泣いてくれるな 입다물어 줘, 더 울지 말아 줘; 待ってくれ、頼む 기다려 줘, 부탁한다), is the request 줘 in a quote, or before another request, order or prohibition in its sentence; and くれるな after a て form forbids the act, -지 말아 줘 (もう泣いてくれるな 이제 울지 말아 줘; spec LEX-4766), not the exclamation 주는구나; after 言って only with a word of forbidding before it (kure-forbid-cue: そんなことを言ってくれるな 그런 말을 하지 말아 줘), since 言ってくれるな alone remarks on what was said (なかなか言ってくれるな 꽤 말해 주는구나).

column3: An address after the word in its sentence: a request that ends it, a prohibition or a question.

The や after a person (not the speaker, a listener or third-person pronoun, nor a title of honour: 先生や) that opens its clause before a comma calls that person (民や、だまっておくれ 백성아, 입다물어 줘; spec LEX-4766) when an address follows in the sentence (vocative-address): (아)야, not the (이)나 of a list (りんごや、みかんを買った 사과나, 귤을 샀다), whose next item is a noun with a case particle after the comma (母や、姉に聞いてください 어머니나, 언니에게).

column3: A verbal noun + しかけている or しかけてる (崩壊しかけてる, read 하기 시작하고 있다) is about to happen, -려 하고 있다 (計画が崩壊しかけてる 계획이 붕괴하려 하고 있다), like the past しかけた of lc3i-shikake; not after a noun that also takes 仕掛ける. A verbal noun of noun.befalls-plan (頓挫) befalls a plan, so its する is 되다 (計画が頓挫した 계획이 좌절되었다; 頓挫しかけてる 좌절되려 하고 있다; 頓挫しかけた 좌절될 뻔했다) (spec GRM-201).

column3: The ない-adjective 間に合わない is read with the verb 늦다 ($Ky@), whose present the adjective's endings in 다 do not give: an ending that starts with 1다 starts with 1는다 (もう間に合わない 이제 늦는다, 間に合わないという話だ 늦는다는 이야기다, 間に合わないなんて 늦는다니; spec LEX-4768), but the 1다 that ends a quote without a period, which casual speech takes (「もう間に合わない」 「이제 늦어」, 「ここからじゃ間に合わないっ！ 「여기에서는 늦어!); its other endings are the verb's own (늦죠, 늦네).
